title: Finite classical Weil diagrams descend to supplied free-system stages
statement: Fix D,l,Omega,Y0 and R as above, and any family P0 of normalized diagram stages for R. For finite vertex, arrow and equation types I,A,J, source and target maps, typed word expressions e,f, classical Weil objects M and arrows a satisfying the geometric-fibre equations, there are a finite E, Weil objects N for the raw operation of P0 E, arrows b and classical Weil identifications beta. The beta intertwine b and a, and all the signed expression equations hold in the underlying raw rational finite-system Hom groups. No sf image equations, coefficient coherence, common-stage lissity or prescribed-object lifts are asserted.

source.place: Weil II (1.1.1)b--d; Stanford L19 Proposition 1.1.9; BS 6.8.4(1),(4); parent steps 2--3 and 7--8

proof.text: Represent the finitely many objects in a common finite coefficient field. Enlarge for all arrows, Weil maps, inverses and the finitely many pullbacks in the words. Geometric fibres jointly detect sheaf map equality. The directed Hom colimit realizes eventual equality, so enlarge once for all listed equations, inverse identities and equivariance squares.

The noetherian geometric base has finitely many clopen connected components. On each nonempty component choose a geometric point. The lisse dictionary and compact-group stable lattice theorem give finite free stable lattices for the underlying monodromy representations. Their finite reductions give normalized free systems; assemble them over the clopen components. Transport rational arrows without demanding integral preservation. The raw pullback map formula and finite_unit of the supplied stage identify actual Frobenius sources and lift Weil structures, inverses and equivariance. Faithfulness of the classical model at the finite field reflects all signed word equations. Empty diagrams use the base coefficient field, and zero/empty components use zero systems.
